title: Aster DM Quality Care Ltd - 540975 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: Aster DM Quality Care Q1 FY27 proforma revenue rose 20% YoY to INR 2,597 Cr, with EBITDA up 30% to INR 576 Cr and margin at 22.2%.
summary.overview: First earnings call after the Aster DM Healthcare and Quality Care merger, effective 1 July 2026, so combined figures are proforma. Growth was volume-led, with over 2 million patients (up 13% YoY) and blended occupancy up 510 bps to 64%. Mature units (73% of revenue) grew 19% with 30% EBITDA margin, while Emerging units grew 63%. Management reiterated a 24-25% margin target within two to three years and a 10-15% synergy target, and said synergy benefits have not yet started to flow.

financial_highlights.change: Aster net cash INR 511 Cr; Quality Care debt INR 1,673 Cr

segments.name: Mature units
segments.commentary: 73% of revenue, grew 19% YoY on higher ARPP IP, better payor mix and MVT; EBITDA +29%, margin about 30% (+230 bps).

segments.name: Focus units
segments.commentary: 15% of revenue, revenue +16% YoY; EBITDA +20%, margin +60 bps. Management says these are running in the teens on EBITDA and need work.

segments.name: Emerging units
segments.commentary: Revenue +63% YoY; EBITDA +240%, margin 12.4% (+640 bps). Kasaragod reached EBITDA breakeven in June 2026, about 9 months after opening.

segments.name: Medical Value Travel (MVT)
segments.commentary: Revenue +62% YoY on new geographies; contribution still low versus peers, with management targeting double-digit share over a couple of years.

guidance_outlook: EBITDA margin target of 24-25% in two to three years post-merger; management said FY29 was not the right framing and expects a good exit in 2027 with targets reached between FY28 and FY29.
Synergy target of 10-15% incremental EBITDA, calculated on FY24 proforma EBITDA (about INR 150-200 Cr). Management reaffirmed it and said synergy benefits should show from this financial year.
Organic framework of 5-6% volume growth and 7-8% ARPP growth, which management says supports the margin target.
No quarterly or annual margin guidance will be given.
MVT growth expected to stay above 50% YoY.
Bed capacity to rise by about 4,170 beds over 3-4 years to over 15,000 beds; 53% brownfield-led.
capex_capacity: Trivandrum (Aster Capital) hospital expected to be operational in H2 FY27, around January 2027.
Hyderabad hospital expected to be operational around April 2027; medical equipment ordering to begin in 1-2 months.
Sarjapur (Bengaluru) facility of more than 450 beds in two blocks; phase I (Block A) expected in H2 FY28.

Cancer centre in Raipur to be inaugurated mid-August 2026. Bhubaneswar is a major project; Kottayam bed additions in 2028, with Nagercoil, Banjara Hills, Nampally and Shifa bed additions also planned.
Aster Women & Children block (159 beds) commissioned in April 2026 at Aster Whitefield, Bengaluru.
demand_pricing: Volume-led growth: Aster patient throughput +16% and ARPP IP +10%; in Kerala, IP volumes +16% and OP volumes +19%.
Robotics volumes up about 80% YoY; joint replacements +39%; transplants +19%. Orthopaedics, Neurology and Oncology each grew over 24%.
Karnataka recovered from single-digit growth in FY26 to about 16% in Q1, with 5-6% volume growth; 18+ doctors added in Bengaluru in Q1.
Management attributed Karnataka and Maharashtra softness to neighbourhood competition, expected to be temporary.
Medcity (Kerala) crossed INR 100 Cr revenue in two months of Q1 (as stated).

qa_highlights.question: How is the merged entity structured across the four clusters and the three India CEOs?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said clusters are based on geographic and business continuity, with parts of Kerala and Maharashtra grouped together and Andhra, Telangana, Central and part of East grouped. Clinical specialties and maturity cuts are being run as a matrix alongside the country CEOs.

qa_highlights.question: Is 24-25% margin achievable in FY27 after the strong start?
qa_highlights.answer: The CFO declined to guide quarterly or yearly margins and said the company is on track for 24-25% in two to three years post-merger.

qa_highlights.question: What low-hanging margin levers remain, and what synergies are realistic?
qa_highlights.answer: Varun Khanna said merger synergies have not yet played out; cohesive working started only in July. The 10-15% incremental EBITDA target is unchanged, with significant results expected from this financial year and annualising next year.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 19-20% growth in Bengaluru sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: The CFO said growth in the lower-to-mid teens, or double digits, is sustainable. He added that competition dips typically last one or two quarters and that a general surgery team that had left has rejoined.

qa_highlights.question: Why is Maharashtra and Karnataka growing slower than the company average?
qa_highlights.answer: The CFO attributed Kerala's recovery to volume-led growth after the Q4 FY25 decline. Karnataka's slower growth was tied to doctor attrition in FY26 and competition, and management said it is now recovering.

qa_highlights.question: What are the timelines for the greenfield projects in Trivandrum, Hyderabad and Sarjapur?
qa_highlights.answer: Trivandrum is expected around January 2027 (H2 FY27), Hyderabad around April 2027, and Sarjapur phase I in H2 FY28.

risks_watch: Synergy delivery: 10-15% incremental EBITDA (INR 150-200 Cr) is still to be proven; management said results start in FY27.
Competitive intensity in Bengaluru and other micro-markets, which hit Karnataka growth earlier.
Merger execution: new leadership structure (three India CEOs, four maturity cuts) is still being finalised; reporting will change, with geographic data to follow in about a quarter.
Focus units (15% of revenue) are in the teens on EBITDA and need to reach mature levels.
Net debt of INR 1,162 Cr combined, with Quality Care carrying INR 1,673 Cr debt, and the INR 114 Cr exceptional cost.
Greenfield timelines (Trivandrum, Hyderabad, Sarjapur) and the Kasaragod ramp are key next-quarter milestones.
summary.management_tone: Confident on operating momentum and recovery in Kerala and Karnataka, but cautious and non-committal on near-term margin and synergy quantification. Management declined quarterly guidance and said merger synergies have not yet started.
key_quotes: Considering that the merger became effective on July 1, 2026, the numbers pertaining to the combined entity are on proforma basis.
For merged entity, synergies haven't played out.
We had said that about a year back that we hope to bring in 10%-15% incremental EBITDA on account of synergies, and we still stick to that.
I won't say FY29 because it's going to be a transition.

Aster Women & Children block, 159 beds at Aster Whitefield

growth.why: Management guides 24-25% EBITDA margin in 2-3 years, 10-15% synergies (INR 150-200 Cr), MVT growth above 50%, and 4,170+ bed roadmap; capacity specifics with timelines (Trivandrum ~Jan 2027, Hyderabad ~Apr 2027) are partial, while margin and synergy targets lack detailed build-up and no revenue growth number is guided.
